## Architecture Definition

The centralised-hydrogen architecture retains the conventional turbine
electrical chain and AC infield collection system. Electricity is aggregated
and converted to hydrogen on one integrated offshore platform. Hydrogen is
then compressed, exported through a subsea pipeline, and handed over at the
defined onshore hydrogen delivery point.

The physical boundary includes the wind turbines and support structures, AC
collection, the integrated central platform, compression, pipeline export, and
the onshore hydrogen-delivery interface. It ends at that connection; the
onshore hydrogen backbone itself is outside the boundary.

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-height: 1.2
flowchart LR
  A["Wind turbine"] --> B["Turbine electrical conversion"]
  B --> C["AC infield collection"]
  C --> D["One integrated offshore platform"]
  D --> E["Hydrogen compression"]
  E --> F["Hydrogen pipeline export"]
  F --> G["Onshore hydrogen-backbone connection"]
```

## Integrated Offshore Platform Boundary

The architecture contains one physical offshore platform. The platform
integrates:

- AC collection and aggregation
- electrolyser transformers and rectifiers
- PEM stack modules
- non-electrical electrolyser balance of plant
- seawater intake, desalination, and electrolyser-grade water treatment

Compression is a separate downstream functional and accounting subsystem. It
is physically hosted on the same platform but is not included in the
electrolyser or balance-of-plant component boundary. This distinction keeps
compression cost and energy consumption separate from hydrogen-production
equipment.

## Included Physical Functions

| Function | Treatment | Canonical owner |
|---|---|---|
| Wind-energy capture and generation | Included | [Wind Turbine](../turbine_system/wind_turbine.qmd) |
| Turbine support structure | Included | [Foundation](../turbine_system/foundation.qmd) |
| Turbine rectification, inversion, and transformation | Included | [Wind Turbine Mass and Cost](../turbine_system/wind_turbine.qmd) |
| AC infield collection | Included | [Infield AC Cables](../electrical_infra/infield_ac_cables.qmd) |
| Central AC aggregation and platform structure | Included on the integrated platform | [Platform Material CAPEX](../platforms/platform_material_capex.qmd) |
| Electrolyser power conversion | Included on the integrated platform | [Electrolyser Power Electronics](../hydrogen_production/elx_power_electronics.qmd) |
| PEM stacks | Included on the integrated platform | [PEM Electrolyser Stack](../hydrogen_production/stack.qmd) |
| Water treatment and non-electrical BOP | Included within the electrolyser facility | [Balance of Plant](../hydrogen_production/balance_of_plant.qmd) |
| Hydrogen compression | Included as a separate subsystem on the platform | [Compressor](../hydrogen_infra/compressor.qmd) |
| Hydrogen export pipeline | Included | [Hydrogen Pipelines](../hydrogen_infra/hydrogen_pipelines.qmd) |
| Onshore backbone-connection interface | Included | [Hydrogen Infrastructure](../hydrogen_infra/overview.qmd) |

Installation of the turbines, foundations, AC collection system, platform, and
pipeline remains inside the economic boundary. Installation assumptions are
maintained in the [Offshore Installation](../offshore_installation/overview.qmd)
section.

## Excluded Functions

The following functions are outside this architecture:

- offshore and onshore HVDC conversion
- HVDC cable export
- turbine-integrated electrolysis
- hydrogen infield pipelines between turbines
- the onshore hydrogen backbone beyond the project connection
- downstream hydrogen storage, distribution, reconversion, and end use

## Architecture Interfaces

| Interface | Boundary definition |
|---|---|
| Turbine to infield network | The conventional turbine electrical chain supplies the AC collection network. |
| Infield network to platform | AC feeders terminate at the single central platform. |
| Electrical collection to electrolysis | Platform power electronics convert collected AC power for the PEM stacks. |
| Electrolyser facility to compression | Produced and conditioned hydrogen leaves the electrolyser boundary and enters the separately accounted compressor subsystem. |
| Compression to export | Compressed hydrogen enters the export pipeline. |
| Export to backbone | The project ends at the defined onshore hydrogen delivery point. |

## Reported Result

The architecture reports installed capital intensity in
EUR~2025~/kW of installed wind-turbine rated capacity. Annual hydrogen cost is
reported in EUR~2025~/MWh-H2-HHV landed at the defined onshore hydrogen
delivery point and in EUR~2025~/kg-H2. These are Tier 1 carrier-product metrics,
not equivalent electricity end-use prices.

## Economic Boundary

The architecture cost includes the common offshore wind project and every
centralised-hydrogen asset and lifecycle activity represented by the shared
cost schema. The one-platform definition prevents the AC
collection platform and electrolyser platform from being counted as separate
physical structures. Component costs remain separately owned even where the
equipment shares that platform.

The hydrogen backbone and any downstream reinforcement or conditioning are
outside the Tier 1 boundary. Development, shared engineering, insurance and
owner contingency remain unresolved shared fields; construction finance, taxes
and financing fees are excluded by the simple-CRF convention. The reporting
contract is defined on
[System Boundary and Carrier-Cost Metrics](../methodology/system_boundary_and_lcoe.qmd).
